correctness.rationale: Direct spectral solution of Landweber gives exact pixel-noise coefficients q^i u_ij/C. For each fixed r, off-diagonal ratios vanish at q^{-1} and q^{-3} rates, proving joint convergence to independent standard Gaussian scores. Lemma 3.4 bias upper bound is checked from scalar maximization, and its ratio to standard deviation vanishes. Selection coverage equals intersection of all r marginal covering events, giving (1-alpha)^r. The checker tests the matrix recurrence, Householder singular spectrum and finite-r Gaussian behavior; it is not substituted for the asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The general difference between marginal and simultaneous inference is classical and is expressly not claimed as new. A full-read of the motivating 2026 source shows its stopping depends on known noise and operator only, unlike the adversarial observation-dependent first-exclusion rule. Earlier adaptive inverse-problem stopping treats risk, and simultaneous inverse-problem inference addresses other collections. No inspected source or searched published result proved the specific r-mode Landweber one-pixel covariance decoupling and limiting selected-coverage law; unindexed equivalent results remain a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: Historical multiple-testing literature could contain the same spectral example using alternative terminology.
Only bounded source examination and semantic search were possible; unindexed and inaccessible papers may exist.
The novelty is the explicit Landweber construction and limit, not the generic observation that multiple peeking harms coverage.

value.rationale: A pixelwise interval can remain individually calibrated at every iteration while observed-data-based selection can make its reported coverage arbitrarily small using no additional measurements. Exact spectral construction supplies a concrete boundary for when numerical uncertainty statements require joint/anytime-valid coverage, not just fixed-k covariance calculations. The target is practically motivated by proposed inverse-problem uncertainty quantification but the deliberately adversarial first-exclusion rule is explicitly distinguished from the original offline stopping design.
